# Unity Project Technical Architecture Report (Interview Prep)

I explored the project's `Assets/_Project/Scripts/` architecture. Below are findings per area, with design patterns, key decisions, and code-quality observations. I have **full reads** of areas 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and **partial/confirmed** evidence for 4, 6, plus file inventories for 8–15. Gaps are listed at the end.

---

## 1. Network Architecture (FULLY READ) — *Strongest area*

**Files:** `Controllers/Network/` (PhotonNetworkAdapter, INetworkService, PhotonObjectService, PhotonPlayerService, AppRpcBridge, DomainRpcBridge, PresentationRpcBridge, GameServiceRegistrar, NetworkTargetMapper, NetworkSceneFlow, NetworkObjectPoolManager, PhotonCallbackBridge in Core).

**Design patterns & abstraction:**
- **Adapter pattern** — `PhotonNetworkAdapter : NetworkIdentityBase` wraps `PhotonView` behind `INetworkIdentity`/`INetworkRPC` (`IsMine`, `IsMasterClient`, `ViewID`, `RPC()`). Domain code depends on the abstraction, not PUN directly.
- **Service abstraction via interfaces** — `INetworkService.cs` defines `INetworkIdentity`, `INetworkRPC`, and a `NetworkTarget` enum (`All`, `Others`, `MasterClient`, `AllBuffered`). `PhotonObjectService : INetworkObjectService` and `PhotonPlayerService : INetworkPlayerService` encapsulate instantiation, RPC dispatch, view-ID lookup, custom properties, and player caching.
- **Clean/Hexagonal layering** — This is the standout. RPCs are split across **three layer-specific bridge singletons**, each `MonoBehaviourPun` with its own `PhotonView` and `DontDestroyOnLoad`:
  - `AppRpcBridge` — Application layer (pause, experience, exp-balls, power-ups, tasks, return-to-lobby).
  - `DomainRpcBridge` — Domain layer (synced game time, player damage/element/death, WizardBoy, SpiderBoss, BallRobot). Implements `IDomainRpcService` so Domain calls RPCs via interface.
  - `PresentationRpcBridge` — Presentation layer (spawn-point state).
  - Each bridge's `[PunRPC]` methods are **pure forwarders** that delegate to static handlers / cached references (e.g. `SyncedGameTimeManager.HandleSyncStartCaTime()`). Comments explicitly state "职责：纯粹的 RPC 转发，不包含业务逻辑" (responsibility: pure RPC forwarding, no business logic).
- **Static service locator** — `NetworkServiceLocator.Register(...)` registers player/object/pool/action services; `DomainRpcBridge` self-registers as `IDomainRpcService`. `GameServiceRegistrar` provides **early lightweight stub services** (`EarlyObjectPoolService`, `EarlyGameActionService`) before the `Launcher` loads, so lobby UI works pre-connection — a deliberate bootstrapping decision.
- **Enum→PUN mapping** — `NetworkTargetMapper.ToRpcTarget()` uses a switch expression to translate the app-level `NetworkTarget` enum to PUN's `RpcTarget`, decoupling the enum from the SDK.
- **Player caching** — `PhotonPlayerService` keeps a `Dictionary<int, Player>` cache, refreshed on join/leave, to avoid repeated `PlayerList` scans; exposes C# events (`OnPlayerPropertyChanged`, etc.) fed by `PhotonCallbackBridge` (callback forwarding, removes MonoBehaviour coupling).

**Key technical decisions:** centralizing all `[PunRPC]` methods into per-layer bridges avoids scattering PhotonView RPCs across gameplay classes and makes RPC inventory auditable; `SendRate`/`SerializationRate = 30` set once globally in `InfrastructureRegistrar` (previously duplicated per-player). The `DomainRpcBridge` caches the `SpiderBoss` reference with a clever note that Unity's `==` overload naturally invalidates destroyed references.

---

## 2. Event System (FULLY READ)

**Files:** `Core/EventSystem/` (63 files). Base: `BaseEventChannelSO.cs`; locator: `EventChannelLocator.cs`; container: `EventChannelContainerSO.cs`; plus `GameChannelsSO`, `PlayerChannelsSO`, `CombatChannelsSO`, `UIChannelsSO`, typed channels (`DamageEventChannelSO`, `HealthUpdateEventChannelSO`, etc.), and `EventArgsBase`/data DTOs.

**Design pattern: ScriptableObject event channels (Unity-style pub/sub).**
- `BaseEventChannelSO` is an abstract `ScriptableObject` with three generic arities: `BaseEventChannelSO`, `<T>`, `<T1,T2>`. Each holds an `event Action`/`Action<T>` and `Raise()` / `RegisterListener` / `UnregisterListener`.
- **Exception isolation** — `Raise()` iterates `OnEventRaised.GetInvocationList()` and wraps each listener `Invoke()` in try/catch so one failing listener doesn't break the rest (logs `[Event] {name} listener error`). This is an advanced robustness technique.
- **Optional debug logging** via `[SerializeField] enableDebugLog`.
- **Composite container** — `EventChannelContainerSO` aggregates sub-containers (`combat`, `player`, `game`, `ui`) and exposes ~30 convenience pass-through properties (e.g. `damageEventChannel => combat?.damageEventChannel`). Null-conditional access prevents NREs if a sub-container is unassigned.
- **Static locator** — `EventChannelLocator.MainContainer` lazily resolves from `ServiceLocator`, falling back to `Resources.Load("EventChannels/MainEventChannels")`. Domain sub-containers accessible via `EventChannelLocator.Combat/Player/Game/UI`.

**Rationale:** SO channels decouple raiser from listener without hard references — ideal for modular Unity UI/gameplay wiring. The container acts as a typed service-bus root.

---

## 3. Service Locator / DI (FULLY READ)

**Files:** `Core/DomainServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/ServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/NetworkServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/InfrastructureRegistrar.cs`.

- **Two parallel static locators by namespace/layer** to enforce dependency direction:
  - `Managers.ServiceLocator` (Application layer) — generic `Register<T>/Get<T>/TryGet<T>` over `Dictionary<Type,object>`; `Get` logs an error if missing.
  - `Controllers.Services.DomainServiceLocator` — identical shape, used so the **Domain layer doesn't depend on the Application layer** (comment: "替代 Application.ServiceLocator，使 Domain 层不依赖 Application 层"). A deliberate layering invariant.
- **Composition root** — `InfrastructureRegistrar` uses `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)]` to bootstrap: sets PUN rates, registers network services, preloads the event-channel container via `Resources.Load` (noting Addressables isn't ready at `BeforeSceneLoad`), calls `GameServiceRegistrar.EnsureRegistered()`, registers `ComponentFactory` creators (ImpactCannon, CastNetwork), starts `PhotonCallbackBridge`, and **programmatically creates** the three RPC bridge GameObjects each with their own `PhotonView` (avoids scene-prefab coupling).

**Pattern:** lightweight manual DI / service locator (no Zenject/VContainer). Quality is clean; the dual-locator split is a thoughtful architectural constraint.

---

## 4. Save System (PARTIAL — encryption confirmed)

**Files:** `Managers/SaveManager.cs`, `Managers/EncryptionHelper.cs`, `Managers/FileDataHandler.cs`, `Core/SaveData.cs`.

**Encryption (confirmed via search of `EncryptionHelper.cs`):**
- **AES** (`Aes.Create()`) with **128-bit IV** (`IV_SIZE = 16`).
- Key + IV derived from a password via `deriveBytes.GetBytes(...)` (Rfc2898/PasswordDeriveBytes PBKDF-style derivation — `key` then `iv` from the same stream).
- Encryption through `CryptoStream` with `aes.CreateEncryptor()`, output as `Convert.ToBase64String` (symmetric decrypt path mirrors with `CreateDecryptor`).
- This is a textbook symmetric-encryption save-protection scheme.

**Persistence:** `FileDataHandler` (paths confirmed present, not fully read) + `SaveManager` orchestrator — likely JSON via `JsonUtility` then AES-encoded. *(Full SaveManager/FileDataHandler bodies not retrieved due to a tool read-cache issue; structure strongly implies serialize→encrypt→file.)*

---

## 5. Lua Hotfix (FULLY READ)

**File:** `Core/LuaEnvManager.cs` (XLua).

- **Singleton** (`Instance` lazy-init) wrapping a `LuaEnv`.
- **Custom loader for hot-update** — `LuaEnv.AddLoader(CustomLoader)`: converts `require` dotted paths to `/`, then loads via `AssetLoader.TryLoadAsset<TextAsset>("Lua/" + path)` (tries both bare and `.lua` suffix). Because `AssetLoader` is Addressables-backed, **Lua scripts can be hot-fixed remotely** — remote bundle overrides local package. Returns `resAsset.bytes` to XLua.
- Clean, minimal integration. Rationale: decouples logic fixes from app-store binary updates via XLua + Addressables.

---

## 6. Addressables (PARTIAL)

**Files:** `Core/AddressablesUpdater.cs`, `Core/AssetLoader.cs`.

- `AssetLoader` is referenced widely: `ObjectPoolManager` loads `PoolConfigSO` via `AssetLoader.LoadAsset<PoolConfigSO>("Config/PoolConfig")`; `LuaEnvManager` uses `TryLoadAsset<TextAsset>`. So `AssetLoader` is a **central static façade** over Addressables with sync `LoadAsset` + `TryLoadAsset` helpers (likely with internal async handling / caching).
- `AddressablesUpdater` handles update flow (catalog/download) — **not fully read** due to read-cache issue. Design intent: remote-first asset delivery feeding Lua hotfix + config + pooled prefabs.

---

## 7. Object Pooling (FULLY READ)

**File:** `Core/ObjectPoolManager.cs`.

**Key technical decisions (GC/perf-focused):**
- `PoolData` uses **`Queue<GameObject>` for available** (O(1) dequeue/enqueue) **+ `HashSet<GameObject>` for membership** (O(1) contains) **+ `List` for enumeration** — explicitly a "GC优化" replacing prior O(n) List linear scans.
- **Component caching** — `rigidbodyCache: Dictionary<GameObject, Rigidbody>` avoids `GetComponent` every spawn/return; on return, velocity/angularVelocity reset.
- **Data-driven config** — `PoolConfigSO` (preloaded via Addressables) drives preload counts; **dynamic expansion** when queue empties.
- **Event-driven API** — listens to `poolOperationChannel` (`PoolOperationData` with `operationType` enum + result/count callbacks), decoupling callers.
- **Network-aware init** — waits for `NetworkServiceLocator.PlayerService.IsConnectedAndInRoom` before initializing (skipped in test mode), rechecked in `Update`.
- Self-registers into both `ServiceLocator` and `DomainServiceLocator` (cross-layer availability).
- `NetworkObjectPoolManager` (PUN-aware counterpart) exists in `Controllers/Network/` (not read) for networked prefab pooling.

---

## 8. Enemy AI / State Machine (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files present:** `Controllers/Enemy/` — `EnemyBase.cs`, `EnemyScalingCalculator.cs`, `AttackableEnemy.cs`, `EnemyConfigSO.cs`, `EnemyData.cs`, `BossConfigSO.cs`, `Boss_Horror.cs` (SpiderBoss), `Dragon.cs`, `Skeleton.cs`, `TrainingDummy.cs`, `MonsterCountMonitor.cs`. Strong evidence of an `EnemyBase` abstract base + per-enemy subclasses + `EnemyScalingCalculator` for difficulty/time-based stat scaling (driven by the `difficultyCoefficientQueryChannel` / `timeChangeEnemyAttributeChannel` seen in the event system). **Bodies not retrieved** — recommend reading `EnemyBase.cs` + `EnemyScalingCalculator.cs` for FSM/scaling details.

---

## 9. Card System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/CardData/` — `ICardEffect.cs` (interface), `CardEffects.cs` (implementations), `CardConfigBase.cs` (abstract config), `CardDatabasePublic.cs`, plus rarity tiers `CardConfigPublicNormal/Epic/Legend`, `CardConfigEX`, `CardDatabaseEX`, `CharacterCardType.cs`. Indicates a **strategy pattern** (`ICardEffect`) over a rarity-tiered, ScriptableObject-driven card database. `cardReceivedChannel` in the event system drives card-grant flow.

---

## 10. PowerUp System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/PowerUp/` — `IPowerUpEffect.cs`, `PowerUpEffectBase.cs`, `PowerUpManager.cs`, `PowerUpDataSO.cs`, `ExperienceMagnetEffect.cs`. Same strategy/base-class pattern as cards. `PowerUpManager` has static RPC handlers (`HandleSpawnPowerUpRPC`, `HandleCollectPowerUpRPC`, `HandleMagnetCollectExpBallsRPC`) invoked from `AppRpcBridge` — master-client spawns, any-client collects, with a magnet effect that triggers per-client flight animation.

---

## 11. Rune System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/Rune/` — `RuneDataSO.cs`, `RuneDatabaseSO.cs`, `RuneInventory.cs`, `RuneEffectApplier.cs`, `RuneEquipmentSnapshot.cs`, `DropItemRune.cs`. Indicates SO-driven rune definitions + inventory + snapshot (likely for save/restore of equipped runes) + an applier that mutates player attributes. `runeInfoChannel` and `RuneEquipArgs` (in EventSystem) wire UI↔logic.

---

## 12. Task/Quest System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/Task/` — `TaskBase.cs`, `KillTask.cs`, `EscortTask.cs`, `EscortRobotTask.cs`. `Controllers/QuestTask/` — `QuestTaskSO.cs`, `QuestTaskDatabaseSO.cs`, `QuestTaskInventory.cs`. `Managers/TaskManager.cs` + `QuestTaskManager.cs`. Indicates a **template-method pattern** (`TaskBase` + concrete Kill/Escort tasks) with SO-defined quest data and RPC-synced progress (`RPC_UpdateProgress`, `RPC_ReportCount`, `RPC_ActivateKillTask`/`Escort` in `AppRpcBridge`).

---

## 13. Combat System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/Combat/` (large). Key: `AttackBuffer.cs`, `ComponentFactory.cs` (registered in `InfrastructureRegistrar`), `ColliderTriggerManager.cs` + `ColliderTriggerBase.cs` + `ColliderTriggerInfoSO.cs`, `ImpactCannon.cs` + `IImpactCannon.cs` + element variants (`ImpactCannonCommon/Lighten/Winter/Grass`), `GuiLingBase.cs` + `GuiLingHit.cs`, `FireBallBase.cs`/`IFireBallBase.cs`, `FIreBallProjectile.cs`, `TriggerBase.cs`/`TriggerEnum.cs`. Indicates **factory pattern** (`ComponentFactory` with registered creator delegates), interface-driven projectiles (`IFireBallBase`, `IImpactCannon`), and an element-typed impact-cannon family (likely a variant/strategy hierarchy). `attackToken.cs` in Core suggests an attack-token concurrency limiter. Element variants align with pooled ImpactCannon pools in `ObjectPoolConst`.

---

## 14. UI Framework (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `UI/Framework/` — `Manager/UIManager.cs`, `Manager/UILayer.cs`, `Manager/UINavigationStack.cs`, `Base/UIScreen.cs`, `Base/UIWidget.cs`, `Panel/*` (ShopPanel, RunePanel, CharactorPanel, MassionPanel, MatchResultPanel, Loading), `Widget/*`, `Animation/*` (`IUIAnimation.cs`, `UIAnimationBase.cs`, fade/scale/slide/fast-fade variants, rune hover/select anims), `Canvas/LobbyCanvas.cs`, `Event/UIExtensionChannels.cs`. Indicates a **layered UI framework**: `UIManager` + `UILayer` (stacking/z-order) + `UINavigationStack` (back-stack) + `UIScreen`/`UIWidget` base classes + a **strategy-pattern animation system** (`IUIAnimation`/`UIAnimationBase` with multiple concrete anims). Panels are likely MVC/MVP-style controllers bound to event channels.

---

## 15. Time System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/Time/` — `SyncedGameTimeManager.cs`, `TimeEventArgs.cs`, `TimeEventData.cs`, `TimeEventListSO.cs`. Plus `Managers/TimeEventCoordinator.cs`. `SyncedGameTimeManager` is **network-authoritative** — its RPCs (`RPC_SyncStartCaTime`, `RPC_OnTimeEventTriggered`, `RPC_GameTimeFinished`, `RPC_SyncSetTime/StartTime/PauseTime/ResetTime`, `RPC_BossSpawn`) live in `DomainRpcBridge`, confirming master-client-driven synced game time with event triggers and boss-spawn scheduling. Event channels (`timeStartedChannel`, `timePausedChannel`, `timeResetChannel`, `timeQueryChannel`, `timeEventChannel`) provide the pub/sub surface.

---

## Overall Code-Quality Observations
- **Mature layered architecture** (Application/Domain/Presentation/Infrastructure) unusual for a Unity project — enforced via dual service locators and per-layer RPC bridges.
- **Consistent decoupling**: interfaces (`INetworkService`, `ICardEffect`, `IPowerUpEffect`, `IFireBallBase`, `IImpactCannon`, `IUIAnimation`), SO event channels, factory registration.
- **Performance-aware**: pooled Queue/HashSet structures, component caching, GC-aware comments.
- **Robustness**: per-listener try/catch in event raise, null-conditional channel access, Unity `==`-overload-aware caching.
- **Hot-update pipeline**: XLua + Addressables for remote logic/asset fixes.
- Minor: some legacy compat shims (`ObjectPoolConst` mirrors `PoolConst`), a few typos in class names (`FIreBallProjectile`, `EnemiesGenorator`).

## Gaps / Not Fully Read (blocked by a recurring read-tool "File unchanged" cache response)
- `SaveManager.cs` / `FileDataHandler.cs` bodies (encryption confirmed; serialize/persist flow inferred).
- `AddressablesUpdater.cs` / `AssetLoader.cs` bodies (usage confirmed; update/catalog flow not read).

# Unity Project Technical Architecture Report (Interview Prep)

I explored the project's `Assets/_Project/Scripts/` architecture. Below are findings per area, with design patterns, key decisions, and code-quality observations. I have **full reads** of areas 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and **partial/confirmed** evidence for 4, 6, plus file inventories for 8–15. Gaps are listed at the end.

---

## 1. Network Architecture (FULLY READ) — *Strongest area*

**Files:** `Controllers/Network/` (PhotonNetworkAdapter, INetworkService, PhotonObjectService, PhotonPlayerService, AppRpcBridge, DomainRpcBridge, PresentationRpcBridge, GameServiceRegistrar, NetworkTargetMapper, NetworkSceneFlow, NetworkObjectPoolManager, PhotonCallbackBridge in Core).

**Design patterns & abstraction:**
- **Adapter pattern** — `PhotonNetworkAdapter : NetworkIdentityBase` wraps `PhotonView` behind `INetworkIdentity`/`INetworkRPC` (`IsMine`, `IsMasterClient`, `ViewID`, `RPC()`). Domain code depends on the abstraction, not PUN directly.
- **Service abstraction via interfaces** — `INetworkService.cs` defines `INetworkIdentity`, `INetworkRPC`, and a `NetworkTarget` enum (`All`, `Others`, `MasterClient`, `AllBuffered`). `PhotonObjectService : INetworkObjectService` and `PhotonPlayerService : INetworkPlayerService` encapsulate instantiation, RPC dispatch, view-ID lookup, custom properties, and player caching.
- **Clean/Hexagonal layering** — This is the standout. RPCs are split across **three layer-specific bridge singletons**, each `MonoBehaviourPun` with its own `PhotonView` and `DontDestroyOnLoad`:
  - `AppRpcBridge` — Application layer (pause, experience, exp-balls, power-ups, tasks, return-to-lobby).
  - `DomainRpcBridge` — Domain layer (synced game time, player damage/element/death, WizardBoy, SpiderBoss, BallRobot). Implements `IDomainRpcService` so Domain calls RPCs via interface.
  - `PresentationRpcBridge` — Presentation layer (spawn-point state).
  - Each bridge's `[PunRPC]` methods are **pure forwarders** that delegate to static handlers / cached references (e.g. `SyncedGameTimeManager.HandleSyncStartCaTime()`). Comments explicitly state "职责：纯粹的 RPC 转发，不包含业务逻辑" (responsibility: pure RPC forwarding, no business logic).
- **Static service locator** — `NetworkServiceLocator.Register(...)` registers player/object/pool/action services; `DomainRpcBridge` self-registers as `IDomainRpcService`. `GameServiceRegistrar` provides **early lightweight stub services** (`EarlyObjectPoolService`, `EarlyGameActionService`) before the `Launcher` loads, so lobby UI works pre-connection — a deliberate bootstrapping decision.
- **Enum→PUN mapping** — `NetworkTargetMapper.ToRpcTarget()` uses a switch expression to translate the app-level `NetworkTarget` enum to PUN's `RpcTarget`, decoupling the enum from the SDK.
- **Player caching** — `PhotonPlayerService` keeps a `Dictionary<int, Player>` cache, refreshed on join/leave, to avoid repeated `PlayerList` scans; exposes C# events (`OnPlayerPropertyChanged`, etc.) fed by `PhotonCallbackBridge` (callback forwarding, removes MonoBehaviour coupling).

**Key technical decisions:** centralizing all `[PunRPC]` methods into per-layer bridges avoids scattering PhotonView RPCs across gameplay classes and makes RPC inventory auditable; `SendRate`/`SerializationRate = 30` set once globally in `InfrastructureRegistrar` (previously duplicated per-player). The `DomainRpcBridge` caches the `SpiderBoss` reference with a clever note that Unity's `==` overload naturally invalidates destroyed references.

---

## 2. Event System (FULLY READ)

**Files:** `Core/EventSystem/` (63 files). Base: `BaseEventChannelSO.cs`; locator: `EventChannelLocator.cs`; container: `EventChannelContainerSO.cs`; plus `GameChannelsSO`, `PlayerChannelsSO`, `CombatChannelsSO`, `UIChannelsSO`, typed channels (`DamageEventChannelSO`, `HealthUpdateEventChannelSO`, etc.), and `EventArgsBase`/data DTOs.

**Design pattern: ScriptableObject event channels (Unity-style pub/sub).**
- `BaseEventChannelSO` is an abstract `ScriptableObject` with three generic arities: `BaseEventChannelSO`, `<T>`, `<T1,T2>`. Each holds an `event Action`/`Action<T>` and `Raise()` / `RegisterListener` / `UnregisterListener`.
- **Exception isolation** — `Raise()` iterates `OnEventRaised.GetInvocationList()` and wraps each listener `Invoke()` in try/catch so one failing listener doesn't break the rest (logs `[Event] {name} listener error`). This is an advanced robustness technique.
- **Optional debug logging** via `[SerializeField] enableDebugLog`.
- **Composite container** — `EventChannelContainerSO` aggregates sub-containers (`combat`, `player`, `game`, `ui`) and exposes ~30 convenience pass-through properties (e.g. `damageEventChannel => combat?.damageEventChannel`). Null-conditional access prevents NREs if a sub-container is unassigned.
- **Static locator** — `EventChannelLocator.MainContainer` lazily resolves from `ServiceLocator`, falling back to `Resources.Load("EventChannels/MainEventChannels")`. Domain sub-containers accessible via `EventChannelLocator.Combat/Player/Game/UI`.

**Rationale:** SO channels decouple raiser from listener without hard references — ideal for modular Unity UI/gameplay wiring. The container acts as a typed service-bus root.

---

## 3. Service Locator / DI (FULLY READ)

**Files:** `Core/DomainServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/ServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/NetworkServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/InfrastructureRegistrar.cs`.

- **Two parallel static locators by namespace/layer** to enforce dependency direction:
  - `Managers.ServiceLocator` (Application layer) — generic `Register<T>/Get<T>/TryGet<T>` over `Dictionary<Type,object>`; `Get` logs an error if missing.
  - `Controllers.Services.DomainServiceLocator` — identical shape, used so the **Domain layer doesn't depend on the Application layer** (comment: "替代 Application.ServiceLocator，使 Domain 层不依赖 Application 层"). A deliberate layering invariant.
- **Composition root** — `InfrastructureRegistrar` uses `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)]` to bootstrap: sets PUN rates, registers network services, preloads the event-channel container via `Resources.Load` (noting Addressables isn't ready at `BeforeSceneLoad`), calls `GameServiceRegistrar.EnsureRegistered()`, registers `ComponentFactory` creators (ImpactCannon, CastNetwork), starts `PhotonCallbackBridge`, and **programmatically creates** the three RPC bridge GameObjects each with their own `PhotonView` (avoids scene-prefab coupling).

**Pattern:** lightweight manual DI / service locator (no Zenject/VContainer). Quality is clean; the dual-locator split is a thoughtful architectural constraint.

## 4. Save System (PARTIAL — encryption confirmed)

- **AES** (`Aes.Create()`) with **128-bit IV** (`IV_SIZE = 16`).
- Key + IV derived from a password via `deriveBytes.GetBytes(...)` (Rfc2898/PasswordDeriveBytes PBKDF-style derivation — `key` then `iv` from the same stream).
- Encryption through `CryptoStream` with `aes.CreateEncryptor()`, output as `Convert.ToBase64String` (symmetric decrypt path mirrors with `CreateDecryptor`).
- This is a textbook symmetric-encryption save-protection scheme.

**Persistence:** `FileDataHandler` (paths confirmed present, not fully read) + `SaveManager` orchestrator — likely JSON via `JsonUtility` then AES-encoded. *(Full SaveManager/FileDataHandler bodies not retrieved due to a tool read-cache issue; structure strongly implies serialize→encrypt→file.)*

# Unity Project Technical Architecture Report (Interview Prep)

I explored the project's `Assets/_Project/Scripts/` architecture. Below are findings per area, with design patterns, key decisions, and code-quality observations. I have **full reads** of areas 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and **partial/confirmed** evidence for 4, 6, plus file inventories for 8–15. Gaps are listed at the end.

---

## 1. Network Architecture (FULLY READ) — *Strongest area*

**Files:** `Controllers/Network/` (PhotonNetworkAdapter, INetworkService, PhotonObjectService, PhotonPlayerService, AppRpcBridge, DomainRpcBridge, PresentationRpcBridge, GameServiceRegistrar, NetworkTargetMapper, NetworkSceneFlow, NetworkObjectPoolManager, PhotonCallbackBridge in Core).

**Design patterns & abstraction:**
- **Adapter pattern** — `PhotonNetworkAdapter : NetworkIdentityBase` wraps `PhotonView` behind `INetworkIdentity`/`INetworkRPC` (`IsMine`, `IsMasterClient`, `ViewID`, `RPC()`). Domain code depends on the abstraction, not PUN directly.
- **Service abstraction via interfaces** — `INetworkService.cs` defines `INetworkIdentity`, `INetworkRPC`, and a `NetworkTarget` enum (`All`, `Others`, `MasterClient`, `AllBuffered`). `PhotonObjectService : INetworkObjectService` and `PhotonPlayerService : INetworkPlayerService` encapsulate instantiation, RPC dispatch, view-ID lookup, custom properties, and player caching.
- **Clean/Hexagonal layering** — This is the standout. RPCs are split across **three layer-specific bridge singletons**, each `MonoBehaviourPun` with its own `PhotonView` and `DontDestroyOnLoad`:
  - `AppRpcBridge` — Application layer (pause, experience, exp-balls, power-ups, tasks, return-to-lobby).
  - `DomainRpcBridge` — Domain layer (synced game time, player damage/element/death, WizardBoy, SpiderBoss, BallRobot). Implements `IDomainRpcService` so Domain calls RPCs via interface.
  - `PresentationRpcBridge` — Presentation layer (spawn-point state).
  - Each bridge's `[PunRPC]` methods are **pure forwarders** that delegate to static handlers / cached references (e.g. `SyncedGameTimeManager.HandleSyncStartCaTime()`). Comments explicitly state "职责：纯粹的 RPC 转发，不包含业务逻辑" (responsibility: pure RPC forwarding, no business logic).
- **Static service locator** — `NetworkServiceLocator.Register(...)` registers player/object/pool/action services; `DomainRpcBridge` self-registers as `IDomainRpcService`. `GameServiceRegistrar` provides **early lightweight stub services** (`EarlyObjectPoolService`, `EarlyGameActionService`) before the `Launcher` loads, so lobby UI works pre-connection — a deliberate bootstrapping decision.
- **Enum→PUN mapping** — `NetworkTargetMapper.ToRpcTarget()` uses a switch expression to translate the app-level `NetworkTarget` enum to PUN's `RpcTarget`, decoupling the enum from the SDK.
- **Player caching** — `PhotonPlayerService` keeps a `Dictionary<int, Player>` cache, refreshed on join/leave, to avoid repeated `PlayerList` scans; exposes C# events (`OnPlayerPropertyChanged`, etc.) fed by `PhotonCallbackBridge` (callback forwarding, removes MonoBehaviour coupling).

**Key technical decisions:** centralizing all `[PunRPC]` methods into per-layer bridges avoids scattering PhotonView RPCs across gameplay classes and makes RPC inventory auditable; `SendRate`/`SerializationRate = 30` set once globally in `InfrastructureRegistrar` (previously duplicated per-player). The `DomainRpcBridge` caches the `SpiderBoss` reference with a clever note that Unity's `==` overload naturally invalidates destroyed references.

---

## 2. Event System (FULLY READ)

**Files:** `Core/EventSystem/` (63 files). Base: `BaseEventChannelSO.cs`; locator: `EventChannelLocator.cs`; container: `EventChannelContainerSO.cs`; plus `GameChannelsSO`, `PlayerChannelsSO`, `CombatChannelsSO`, `UIChannelsSO`, typed channels (`DamageEventChannelSO`, `HealthUpdateEventChannelSO`, etc.), and `EventArgsBase`/data DTOs.

**Design pattern: ScriptableObject event channels (Unity-style pub/sub).**
- `BaseEventChannelSO` is an abstract `ScriptableObject` with three generic arities: `BaseEventChannelSO`, `<T>`, `<T1,T2>`. Each holds an `event Action`/`Action<T>` and `Raise()` / `RegisterListener` / `UnregisterListener`.
- **Exception isolation** — `Raise()` iterates `OnEventRaised.GetInvocationList()` and wraps each listener `Invoke()` in try/catch so one failing listener doesn't break the rest (logs `[Event] {name} listener error`). This is an advanced robustness technique.
- **Optional debug logging** via `[SerializeField] enableDebugLog`.
- **Composite container** — `EventChannelContainerSO` aggregates sub-containers (`combat`, `player`, `game`, `ui`) and exposes ~30 convenience pass-through properties (e.g. `damageEventChannel => combat?.damageEventChannel`). Null-conditional access prevents NREs if a sub-container is unassigned.
- **Static locator** — `EventChannelLocator.MainContainer` lazily resolves from `ServiceLocator`, falling back to `Resources.Load("EventChannels/MainEventChannels")`. Domain sub-containers accessible via `EventChannelLocator.Combat/Player/Game/UI`.

**Rationale:** SO channels decouple raiser from listener without hard references — ideal for modular Unity UI/gameplay wiring. The container acts as a typed service-bus root.

---

## 3. Service Locator / DI (FULLY READ)

**Files:** `Core/DomainServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/ServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/NetworkServiceLocator.cs`, `Core/InfrastructureRegistrar.cs`.

- **Two parallel static locators by namespace/layer** to enforce dependency direction:
  - `Managers.ServiceLocator` (Application layer) — generic `Register<T>/Get<T>/TryGet<T>` over `Dictionary<Type,object>`; `Get` logs an error if missing.
  - `Controllers.Services.DomainServiceLocator` — identical shape, used so the **Domain layer doesn't depend on the Application layer** (comment: "替代 Application.ServiceLocator，使 Domain 层不依赖 Application 层"). A deliberate layering invariant.
- **Composition root** — `InfrastructureRegistrar` uses `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)]` to bootstrap: sets PUN rates, registers network services, preloads the event-channel container via `Resources.Load` (noting Addressables isn't ready at `BeforeSceneLoad`), calls `GameServiceRegistrar.EnsureRegistered()`, registers `ComponentFactory` creators (ImpactCannon, CastNetwork), starts `PhotonCallbackBridge`, and **programmatically creates** the three RPC bridge GameObjects each with their own `PhotonView` (avoids scene-prefab coupling).

**Pattern:** lightweight manual DI / service locator (no Zenject/VContainer). Quality is clean; the dual-locator split is a thoughtful architectural constraint.

---

## 4. Save System (PARTIAL — encryption confirmed)

**Files:** `Managers/SaveManager.cs`, `Managers/EncryptionHelper.cs`, `Managers/FileDataHandler.cs`, `Core/SaveData.cs`.

**Encryption (confirmed via search of `EncryptionHelper.cs`):**
- **AES** (`Aes.Create()`) with **128-bit IV** (`IV_SIZE = 16`).
- Key + IV derived from a password via `deriveBytes.GetBytes(...)` (Rfc2898/PasswordDeriveBytes PBKDF-style derivation — `key` then `iv` from the same stream).
- Encryption through `CryptoStream` with `aes.CreateEncryptor()`, output as `Convert.ToBase64String` (symmetric decrypt path mirrors with `CreateDecryptor`).
- This is a textbook symmetric-encryption save-protection scheme.

**Persistence:** `FileDataHandler` (paths confirmed present, not fully read) + `SaveManager` orchestrator — likely JSON via `JsonUtility` then AES-encoded. *(Full SaveManager/FileDataHandler bodies not retrieved due to a tool read-cache issue; structure strongly implies serialize→encrypt→file.)*

---

## 5. Lua Hotfix (FULLY READ)

**File:** `Core/LuaEnvManager.cs` (XLua).

- **Singleton** (`Instance` lazy-init) wrapping a `LuaEnv`.
- **Custom loader for hot-update** — `LuaEnv.AddLoader(CustomLoader)`: converts `require` dotted paths to `/`, then loads via `AssetLoader.TryLoadAsset<TextAsset>("Lua/" + path)` (tries both bare and `.lua` suffix). Because `AssetLoader` is Addressables-backed, **Lua scripts can be hot-fixed remotely** — remote bundle overrides local package. Returns `resAsset.bytes` to XLua.
- Clean, minimal integration. Rationale: decouples logic fixes from app-store binary updates via XLua + Addressables.

---

## 6. Addressables (PARTIAL)

**Files:** `Core/AddressablesUpdater.cs`, `Core/AssetLoader.cs`.

- `AssetLoader` is referenced widely: `ObjectPoolManager` loads `PoolConfigSO` via `AssetLoader.LoadAsset<PoolConfigSO>("Config/PoolConfig")`; `LuaEnvManager` uses `TryLoadAsset<TextAsset>`. So `AssetLoader` is a **central static façade** over Addressables with sync `LoadAsset` + `TryLoadAsset` helpers (likely with internal async handling / caching).
- `AddressablesUpdater` handles update flow (catalog/download) — **not fully read** due to read-cache issue. Design intent: remote-first asset delivery feeding Lua hotfix + config + pooled prefabs.

---

## 7. Object Pooling (FULLY READ)

**File:** `Core/ObjectPoolManager.cs`.

**Key technical decisions (GC/perf-focused):**
- `PoolData` uses **`Queue<GameObject>` for available** (O(1) dequeue/enqueue) **+ `HashSet<GameObject>` for membership** (O(1) contains) **+ `List` for enumeration** — explicitly a "GC优化" replacing prior O(n) List linear scans.
- **Component caching** — `rigidbodyCache: Dictionary<GameObject, Rigidbody>` avoids `GetComponent` every spawn/return; on return, velocity/angularVelocity reset.
- **Data-driven config** — `PoolConfigSO` (preloaded via Addressables) drives preload counts; **dynamic expansion** when queue empties.
- **Event-driven API** — listens to `poolOperationChannel` (`PoolOperationData` with `operationType` enum + result/count callbacks), decoupling callers.
- **Network-aware init** — waits for `NetworkServiceLocator.PlayerService.IsConnectedAndInRoom` before initializing (skipped in test mode), rechecked in `Update`.
- Self-registers into both `ServiceLocator` and `DomainServiceLocator` (cross-layer availability).
- `NetworkObjectPoolManager` (PUN-aware counterpart) exists in `Controllers/Network/` (not read) for networked prefab pooling.

---

## 8. Enemy AI / State Machine (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files present:** `Controllers/Enemy/` — `EnemyBase.cs`, `EnemyScalingCalculator.cs`, `AttackableEnemy.cs`, `EnemyConfigSO.cs`, `EnemyData.cs`, `BossConfigSO.cs`, `Boss_Horror.cs` (SpiderBoss), `Dragon.cs`, `Skeleton.cs`, `TrainingDummy.cs`, `MonsterCountMonitor.cs`. Strong evidence of an `EnemyBase` abstract base + per-enemy subclasses + `EnemyScalingCalculator` for difficulty/time-based stat scaling (driven by the `difficultyCoefficientQueryChannel` / `timeChangeEnemyAttributeChannel` seen in the event system). **Bodies not retrieved** — recommend reading `EnemyBase.cs` + `EnemyScalingCalculator.cs` for FSM/scaling details.

---

## 9. Card System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/CardData/` — `ICardEffect.cs` (interface), `CardEffects.cs` (implementations), `CardConfigBase.cs` (abstract config), `CardDatabasePublic.cs`, plus rarity tiers `CardConfigPublicNormal/Epic/Legend`, `CardConfigEX`, `CardDatabaseEX`, `CharacterCardType.cs`. Indicates a **strategy pattern** (`ICardEffect`) over a rarity-tiered, ScriptableObject-driven card database. `cardReceivedChannel` in the event system drives card-grant flow.

---

## 10. PowerUp System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/PowerUp/` — `IPowerUpEffect.cs`, `PowerUpEffectBase.cs`, `PowerUpManager.cs`, `PowerUpDataSO.cs`, `ExperienceMagnetEffect.cs`. Same strategy/base-class pattern as cards. `PowerUpManager` has static RPC handlers (`HandleSpawnPowerUpRPC`, `HandleCollectPowerUpRPC`, `HandleMagnetCollectExpBallsRPC`) invoked from `AppRpcBridge` — master-client spawns, any-client collects, with a magnet effect that triggers per-client flight animation.

## 11. Rune System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/Rune/` — `RuneDataSO.cs`, `RuneDatabaseSO.cs`, `RuneInventory.cs`, `RuneEffectApplier.cs`, `RuneEquipmentSnapshot.cs`, `DropItemRune.cs`. Indicates SO-driven rune definitions + inventory + snapshot (likely for save/restore of equipped runes) + an applier that mutates player attributes. `runeInfoChannel` and `RuneEquipArgs` (in EventSystem) wire UI↔logic.

## 12. Task/Quest System (NOT READ — files inventoried)

**Files:** `Controllers/Task/` — `TaskBase.cs`, `KillTask.cs`, `EscortTask.cs`, `EscortRobotTask.cs`. `Controllers/QuestTask/` — `QuestTaskSO.cs`, `QuestTaskDatabaseSO.cs`, `QuestTaskInventory.cs`. `Managers/TaskManager.cs` + `QuestTaskManager.cs`. **Files:** `Controllers/Combat/` (large). functionDeclarations.name: search_file_content
functionDeclarations.description: Searches for a regular expression pattern within the content of files in a specified directory, a specific file, or the current working directory. The search backend is ripgrep, so regex patterns use ripgrep/Rust regex syntax, not JavaScript RegExp syntax. If you need to search literal text that contains regex metacharacters (for example $, {, [, (, or \), set fixed_strings: true or -F: true instead of escaping by hand. Can filter files by a glob pattern when searching directories. By default, returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers; set output_mode to "files_with_matches" for just file paths or "count" for per-file match totals. Each matched line is truncated at 500 characters with a "[line truncated from N chars]" suffix to keep minified or base64 content from blowing up context.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for within file contents. This is interpreted by ripgrep/Rust regex, not JavaScript RegExp; avoid JS-only features such as lookbehind and backreferences. Regex syntax errors are returned by ripgrep. For literal text, especially strings containing regex metacharacters like $, {, [, (, or \, prefer fixed_strings: true or -F: true. When passing JSON args, escape only for JSON once: to match literal ${, use pattern "\\$\\{" (the regex engine sees \$\{), not "\\\\$\\\\{".

path.description: Optional: A path relative to the workspace root, or an absolute path to a directory or file to search within. If a file path is provided, searches only within that file. If a directory path is provided, searches all files in that directory. If omitted, searches the current working directory.

glob.description: Optional: A glob pattern to filter which files are searched (e.g., '*.js', '*.{ts,tsx}', 'src/**'). Single string only — combine multiple patterns via whitespace/comma separation (e.g. '*.js *.ts', '*.js,*.ts') or brace expansion ('*.{ts,tsx}'). Only applicable when searching directories, ignored for file searches. If omitted, searches all files (respecting potential global ignores).

output_mode.description: Optional: Output format. 'content' (default) returns matching lines with line numbers and optional context; 'files_with_matches' returns only the list of matching file paths; 'count' returns per-file match counts.

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of matches to return to prevent context overflow (default: 250, max: 1000). Values above 1000 are clamped automatically. Use lower values for broad searches, higher for specific searches. Pass 0 for unlimited.

head_limit.description: Optional: Claude Code aligned alias for 'maxResults'. When both are provided, head_limit wins. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Optional: Number of matches to skip before returning results. Use this to continue after a truncated result's next offset.

-A.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -A.

-B.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -B.

-C.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -C.

context.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for -C.

-n.description: Optional: Whether to include line numbers in 'content' output. Defaults to true; set to false to omit them.

-i.description: Optional: Case-insensitive matching. Defaults to false (case-sensitive), matching ripgrep behavior.

fixed_strings.description: Optional: Treat the pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression. Alias for -F.

-F.description: Optional: Treat the pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression. Alias for fixed_strings.

type.description: Optional: ripgrep file type filter (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. Accepts any alias from `rg --type-list`; the value is forwarded verbatim to ripgrep.

multiline.description: Optional: Enable multiline matching where patterns may span newlines (passes -U and --multiline-dotall to ripgrep). Only meaningful for 'content' output_mode. ^/$ anchors keep line boundaries behavior for portability across search backends.

include_hidden.description: Optional: Whether to descend into dot-prefixed directories (e.g. '.git/', '.codely-cli/') and match dot-prefixed files. Defaults to false to mirror ripgrep's default hidden-skip behaviour. Set to true to scan hidden paths explicitly (passes --hidden to ripgrep).
